applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France has an extensive network of bilateral investment treaties; applicability depends on each investor's nationality, treaty status, and the investment facts.
France has an extensive network of bilateral double taxation agreements; the applicable agreement depends on the tax residence of each relevant person or entity.
Applicable EU instruments may include the EU internal-market and investment-related rules; no specific treaty can be identified without the investor's country of residence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code, Articles L. 561-2 et seq. and L. 561-2-2, including the beneficial-owner identification and customer due-diligence framework; Articles R. 561-1 et seq. define beneficial ownership criteria. French Commercial Code, Articles L. 561-46 and R. 561-55 et seq., govern beneficial-owner declarations filed with the commercial register. Relevant company-law provisions include Commercial Code Articles L. 223-1 et seq. for SARLs. Beneficial-owner filings are made through the applicable one-stop business formalities system and transmitted to the competent register.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Identify and risk-assess politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates under French Monetary and Financial Code Articles L. 561-10 and R. 561-18 et seq.; perform risk-based customer, UBO, source-of-funds, and source-of-wealth checks. Screen against applicable EU and French asset-freeze measures, UN Security Council sanctions, and relevant OFAC lists where required by the transaction, counterparties, or payment rails. OFAC screening is not a universal French statutory requirement. Retain documented screening results and refresh them on a risk-based basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); company formalities are routed to the competent commercial register and RCS.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be stated in the articles of association and filed in the French business formalities system. French names may use permitted Latin-script characters and accents; names must not mislead, infringe third-party rights, or contravene public order. Foreign-language elements and transliterations are not generally prohibited, but the proposed name should be checked for registrability, trademark conflicts, and misleading regulated-sector implications. SARL legal-form designation must appear in company documents as required by law.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words or expressions suggesting a regulated activity or official status where the company lacks the required authorization or could mislead the public
Protected public-authority, state, or institutional designations used without authorization
Third-party company names, trademarks, trade names, and other protected signs where use would infringe rights or create confusion
Terms contrary to public order or good morals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not provide a general statutory company-name reservation period equivalent to a temporary name hold; the value 0 denotes that no fixed reservation window is prescribed. Before filing, search the INPI trademark and company-name resources and relevant RCS records. If a formal filing is rejected, obtain the written decision and reason, correct the filing or submit supporting evidence through the Guichet unique. Use the appeal route and deadline stated in the decision; where the decision is appealable, pursue the competent administrative or judicial remedy as applicable. A name dispute involving prior private rights may require civil proceedings and is not resolved solely by an administrative appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A SARL must have a registered office in France. Domiciliation at a commercial domiciliation provider is generally permissible if the provider holds the required authorization and a compliant written domiciliation agreement is maintained. A manager's residence or suitable business premises may also be used subject to applicable conditions. A virtual office does not replace operational, tax, consumer, employment, data-protection, or banking substance appropriate to the actual business. No sector-specific real-estate license is assumed for the described SaaS scope, but screening or tenant-selection features may trigger separate data-protection, consumer, discrimination, or regulated-activity requirements depending on actual functionality.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable statutory inspection probability is published. An unannounced physical inspection risk cannot be quantified; it is generally fact-specific and may increase with tax, AML, labor, consumer-protection, or suspected fictitious-domicile concerns. Maintain evidence of the right to use the address, accessible records, and actual management and business activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), acting through the competent local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); official operator portals: impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel), ProGres for VAT formalities and filings, plus guichet-entreprises.fr / INPI as the central company registration gateway (RCS / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce). Intra-Community VAT number validation is performed via the EU VIES system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL obtains its INSEE SIREN and SIRET identifiers automatically upon completion of the corporate formation filing with the RCS through the guichet-entreprises.fr single window. The DGFiP subsequently issues the intra-Community VAT number (n° de TVA intracommunautaire) in the format FRxxYYYYYYYYY, where xx is the two-digit control key and YYYYYYYYY is the nine-digit SIREN. A non-resident entity with a French taxable nexus (e.g., supply of e-services to French final consumers, a French permanent establishment, or French real-estate assets) must register directly with the competent SIE using CERFA form No. 1390-CA, or electronically through ProGres; non-EU suppliers without an EU establishment must appoint an accredited French tax representative (représentant fiscal). For pure intra-EU distance sales of SaaS to final consumers, the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) portal may be used from the member state of establishment, avoiding separate French VAT registration while the annual EU-wide €10,000 distance-sales threshold is not exceeded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box regime. Relevant elections and statutory mechanisms: (1) CGI Art. 239 bis AB — a qualifying SARL (all members being natural persons, fewer than 50 employees, annual consolidated turnover below €10 million) may elect, for a maximum of five fiscal years, to be fiscally transparent and taxed at member level under the personal income tax (Impôt sur le Revenu) regime instead of corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés); (2) CGI Art. 223 A — election for the French tax-integration group regime (intégration fiscale), available where a French parent holds at least 95% of the SARL, allowing consolidation of results and neutralization of intragroup transactions; (3) default entity-level taxation at the 25% standard IS rate, with the reduced 15% rate applicable to the first €42,500 of taxable profit of small enterprises (turnover below €10 million). Hybrid mismatch outcomes under the ATAD transposition are neutralized mandatorily in France; no elective hybrid or check-the-box deficiency mechanism is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic franchise en base de TVA thresholds applicable to a French-established SARL: €93,500 annual turnover for supplies of goods and €37,500 for supplies of services (including SaaS and electronically supplied services) as of 1 January 2025; below the applicable threshold the franchise-in-base exemption may apply. Non-established foreign suppliers, whether EU or non-EU, have no registration threshold: French VAT registration is due from the first taxable transaction performed in France. For intra-EU distance sales and e-services to final consumers, the EU-wide €10,000 annual threshold determines recourse to the OSS scheme instead of domestic VAT registration in each destination state.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing and e-reporting under CGI Art. 289 bis, phased as follows: from 1 September 2026 all taxable persons established in France must be capable of receiving e-invoices, and large and mid-size undertakings must issue e-invoices; from 1 February 2027 small and micro-enterprises, including the typical SARL, must issue e-invoices. Invoices must be issued in an approved structured format (Factur-X, UBL, CII) and transmitted through a certified dematerialization platform (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire — PDP) or the public portal (Portail Public de Facturation — PPF), which relays invoice data and e-reporting information (B2B transactions, B2C flows, and payment data) to DGFiP. France does not operate a tax-authority pre-clearance or digital-stamping system; the obligation is a near-real-time data transmission and fiscal-perimeter control regime administered through the PPF.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Pure SaaS and electronically supplied services: (1) B2B supplies to customers established outside France fall outside the scope of French VAT under the place-of-supply rule (CGI Art. 259-1; EU VAT Directive Art. 44), resulting in a de facto 0% French VAT charge with reverse-charge accounting at destination; (2) B2C supplies to non-EU consumers are not subject to French VAT; (3) B2C supplies to consumers in other EU member states are taxed at the destination member state's VAT rate via the OSS portal once the annual EU-wide €10,000 distance-sales threshold is exceeded, while below that threshold domestic French VAT at 20% applies; (4) where tangible goods are exported together with the SaaS (e.g., hardware kiosks, IoT edge devices), zero-rating under CGI Art. 262-I applies provided the goods are physically shipped or dispatched outside the EU within 90 days and the export is documented per the Union Customs Code implementing rules. Input VAT incurred in France (cloud hosting, marketing, professional fees, real-estate-related costs) remains recoverable through the French CA3 VAT return or the cross-border EU VAT refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/ENS lodged via the DELTA customs system) — required only where tangible goods are exported
Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill proving physical dispatch outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT bank credit confirmation evidencing collection and receipt of export consideration
Signed SaaS master agreement, statement of work, and export invoice annotated with reverse-charge or 0% VAT treatment
Customer VAT identification number and VIES/AC validation certificate for foreign B2B customers
Service-performance evidence (application logs, hosting usage reports, delivery and go-live certificates) substantiating provision of the electronic service
Proof of customer establishment abroad (certificate of incorporation or tax residence certificate) demonstrating place of supply outside France
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP verifies export support files, customer identity, and actual repatriation of proceeds; failure to substantiate the export, the customer's foreign establishment, or the collection of funds gives DGFiP the right to claw back all previously recovered input VAT and to re-impose French VAT on the supply, plus late-payment interest (intérêt de retard of 0.20% per month) and penalties: 40% for intentional inaccuracy (manquement délibéré) or 80% for fraud, fictitious exports, or undeclared activity (CGI Arts. 1729, 1730 and 1731). The ordinary reassessment period is three years (LPF Art. L.169), extended to ten years for undisclosed or occult activities and coordinated international fraud. French customs may additionally impose fines for false export declarations, and criminal prosecution for fiscal fraud (escroquerie fiscale) is possible in aggravated invoicing schemes. The French foreign-exchange benchmark requires repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days of the export or contractual payment due date (a contractual term of up to one year may be agreed), and non-repatriation may be treated as a customs and currency offense precipitating immediate VAT re-characterization.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), operating as the national central bank and exercising delegated exchange-control and external financial relations authority on behalf of the French Ministry of Economy, Finance, and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty (Direction Générale du Trésor). The legal framework is codified under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), together with EU-level capital-movement rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a founding Eurozone member and maintains full convertibility for the euro pursuant to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Article 63). Both current-account transactions (trade in services, SaaS subscriptions, property-management fees) and capital-account operations (direct equity injection, dividend distributions, loan repayments) are free of quantitative exchange control. Profit remittance from a French SARL to non-resident shareholders is permissible without prior authorisation, subject to ordinary corporate formalities (annual accounts, AGM approval of dividend distribution), the withholding tax provisions of Article 119 bis of the French General Tax Code, and anti-money-laundering verification. The only practical hurdles arise from documentary compliance—such as proof of corporate authorisation, BO registration, and, where the beneficial owner is located in a FATF-gray-listed jurisdiction, enhanced due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. French exchange-control regulations abolished mandatory surrender or repatriation of export proceeds for both euro and foreign currency transactions. A French exporter may retain balances in foreign currency accounts, whether held with a French resident bank or an non-resident financial institution, subject to the general obligation for all residents to report cross-border transactions to the Banque de France for monetary-statistical purposes. Specifically, when individual cross-border payments exceed EUR 750,000, a declaration to the Banque de France via the dedicated OFA platform is required for the balance-of-payments compilation; this does not constitute permission or exchange-control approval. For VAT and corporate income tax purposes, the business must maintain a clear audit trail linking export invoices to bank receipts, typically provided by a SWIFT MT103 received report and monthly treasury reconciliation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment_quali: Full current-account convertibility and free capital mobility apply within the Eurozone framework. Profit remittance restrictions are of a documentary and tax nature only, not exchange-control origin.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules_qualitat: Zero surrender ratio and zero mandatory conversion timeline exist. Export proceeds may remain in foreign currency indefinitely, provided transfer statistics are reported above the EUR 750,000 annual/payment threshold.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.evidence_documentation_required: K-bis extract, Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) photocopy from the French Trade and Companies Registry, original shareholders' meeting minutes for dividend approvals, statutory auditors' report (when the SARL has a statutory auditor), and valid anti-money-laundering source-of-funds documentation for each remittance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.risk_appetite_profile: Accepts regulated PropTech SaaS entities on managed KYC basis for inbound investor capital; comfortable with non-resident directorship subject to collective beneficial-owner declaration and positive tax references.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.freight_term_rails: SEPA, SWIFT, local currency clearing, API treasury integration via BNP Paribas Corporate Banking.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.banking_channel: Dedicated relationship manager, online corporate banking portal, host-to-host API connectivity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.risk_appetite_profile: Standard low-risk operational account suitable for subscription receivables, ACH/Direct rails if using a US partner, and outbound vendor payments. Full acceptance of a hybrid delivery model (SaaS plus real-estate screening services).
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.freight_term_rails: SEPA Instant, SEPA Credit Transfer, SWIFT, direct debit for receivables, commercial LC issuance service.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.banking_channel: Corporate internet banking, SWIFTNet, file-based Batch API for MT101/MT103.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.risk_appetite_profile: Regional banking relationship with Luxembourg/France network; more cautious on fast-growth SaaS and non-standard ISIC coding, but acceptable if the SARL maintains a French registered office and full FNFP (Fichier National des Flux Paiement) compliance for platforms.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.freight_term_rails: SEPA, SWIFT, high-value payments through the French RTGS system (T2-T2S), local clearing.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.banking_channel: Online corporate portal and direct file exchange; onboarding potentially longer if non-French entities sit in the ownership chain.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: High as a complementary collection and payout layer, Medium as the sole clearing rail. French-licensed and EEA passported Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Stripe Financial Services (Ireland/Netherlands branch), Checkout.com (France), and Lemonway (France) are viable for primary subscription collection, cross-border payout, and embedded PropTech payments. The main legal constraint is the PSD2 safeguarding rule: client funds held by an EMI must be segregated in a protected account at a regulated credit institution or invested in secure liquid assets. The EMI itself cannot operate as a full treasury account, cannot provide lending or cash-pooling, and must be subject to the SARL's contractual terms for merchant-of-record vs. payment-facilitator model. For a low-risk, non-licensed PropTech platform, using an EMI for daily receivables and a domestic commercial bank for capital operations and settlement balance is the optimal tiered banking structure. The French ACPR applies conduct-of-business supervision; the SARL must complete the EMI's risk on-boarding and, when operating a trading platform (real-estate sales), may also need to comply with the Order of 2019 on crowdfunding if payment flows are related to real-estate transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French anti-money-laundering rules (ACPR-AMF guidelines, Directive (EU) 2015/849 as transposed) do not require a statutory face-to-face interview for every corporate director. Article R561-13 of the Monetary and Financial Code permits the use of reliable, independent, remote electronic identification subject to RGPD-compliance and FIDO-level verification. In practice, most established domestic banks (BNP, SocGen) will require that at least one director or a designated compliance officer (signature holder) attend a live video-conference interview and verify his or her identity via a foreign official identity document, proof of residential address (not older than three months), and a preliminary telephone validation. The physical-presence mandate is effectively waived for accounts opened through the bank's remote KYC digital process, but this is only available to having an experienced French director or executive manager. Where the SARL has 100% non-resident shareholders, a minimum physical (or notarised apostilled) signature attendance in front of a French bank advisor is commonly requested to mitigate jurisdiction risk. The bank will also request a sanctioned proof from the register of beneficial owners and the K-bis legalisation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity - ultimate natural-person shareholders are not fully exposed in the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) or the RBE filing is older than 30 days.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the original RBE extract issued by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within the last 30 days, the current K-bis extract, the notarised shareholder register (registre de titres), a signed organisational chart with ultimate beneficial ownership percentages, plus all identification documents of each natural-person BO. If the BO is resident in a high-risk jurisdiction, add a FATF-compliant source-of-wealth affidavit and audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds uncertainty for initial capital injection - equity financing from a non-resident investor or parent routed through a third-country bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply a legally executed capital injection resolution, constitution of the block funds, investor profile form with passport/passport-copy, bank statements from the remitting account (last 3 months), opening bank evidence of the parent's legitimate business, and an explanation of the economic rationale for the transaction. In case of a loan along with equity, add a signed loan agreement (mandatory for remittance), interest-rate calculation, and evidence of overall Solvency/equity-limits compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent-banking red flag due to the 'unusual' combination of a PropTech SaaS (ISIC 6201) with the NAICS 531390 real-estate characteristics - banks see potential facilitation of undisclosed real-estate transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a business-model description, client-facing terms of service, SaaS-scope statement (ISIC 6201 primary), platform AML surveillance assessments, annual revenue split between pure SaaS and real-estate property-management support, evidence that the company does not hold client monies for sale proceeds, and a detailed policy on acceptance of real-estate partners. A supporting legal opinion from a French avocat may accelerate onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of third-party payment processors (Stripe, ACH/Direct) for revenue concentration, triggering a bank's sub-merchant due-diligence review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed agreements with processors, processing-statements showing monthly volumes, client-acquisition records, merchant IDs, and a compliance certificate establishing processor-based KYC/AML. Banks generally accept this if the aggregate flow through the processor does not exceed 40% of total annual revenue and a reconciliation ledger is in place.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.domestic_accounts_recommended_structure: One Capital Escrow Account (BNP Paribas) for inbound equity injections and one Operational Account (Société Générale) for daily operating inflows/outflows, distinct from any EMI settlement balance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.local_statutory_compliance_obligations: For each bank account, the SARL must notify the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) of the existence when asked; report cross-border aggregate transfers to Banque de France when exceeding EUR 750,000; and maintain a cash-management policy compliant with the Eurozone negative interest and liquidity regulations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders shall route investments via SWIFT MT103 using an official EU purpose code identifying the underlying transaction. For capital increases, the recommended code is 'P011 - Domestic transfer from/to abroad (capital contribution)' or, as used by French banks, 'FCAP' in the transaction narrative. The wire must reference the Quick ERN (European Registration Number) of the SARL and the K-bis identification number to enable the bank's automatic reconciliation. The account for inward remittances is the dedicated Capital Escrow Account. If the aggregate cross-border investment (including loans) reaches the French statistical threshold (EUR 15 million annual investment for external trade) or if the SARL is in a sensitive sector (defence etc. - not applicable here), a post-closing declaration to the Economy and Finance Ministry may apply. For any transfer equal to or exceeding EUR 10,000, a documentary anti-money-laundering declaration is embedded in the bank's payment process. A compliance file (purpose, identity, BO) must be pre-submitted to the receiving bank before the wire is awaited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound trade settlements are as follows: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (instant or standard) for euro payments to EU beneficiaries, with beneficiary identification by IBAN and reason codes associated with invoiced SaaS subscription fees; (ii) SWIFT MT103/103+ for non-EEA transfers in foreign currency, including USD and GBP, using highly structured purpose codes; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credit, UCP600) for any real-property-linked cross-border transaction that requires title-vs-payment nexus, using a French issuing bank and a conforming presentation set; and (iv) ACH Direct for US-dollar disbursements, but only where the bank has a US partner and the SARL maintains a US account, considered an ancillary rail. For all outbound payments, the French Tax Administration requires a voucher trail: supplier contract, invoice, verification of economic reality, and, where applicable, an annual report of payments to non-resident beneficiaries exceeding EUR 1,200 (Article 242 ter of the CGI) - the 'Fichier des comptes étrangers.' The SARL must also verify through the EU sanctions lists that the beneficiary is not designated in OFAC/EU annexations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign-exchange forward contracts (Match Principles: EUR/USD or EUR/GBP) transacted with a French licensed credit institution for trade receivables/settlement up to 12 months maturity.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic or restricted currencies, but strictly as hedging of actual underlying commercial flows and with a licensed counterparty in a jurisdiction where NDF markets are permitted (not for EUR-domestic).

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) only for material debt in a currency other than EUR, transacted via the bank's derivatives desk and documented under ISDA Master Agreement with French governing-law protocol.
Currency options (European-style) executed on regulated markets or via an authorised investment firm, limited to 12-month tenors and aligned to forecast paid invoices.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.internal_liquidity_pooling_and_sweeping: The SARL treasury function may use an automated cash concentration service (e.g., Societe Generale's Cash Management plus) to sweep the Operational Account and the EMI merchant account balances into the BNP Capital Escrow Account, provided that the EMI does not restrict early payout and that such sweeping is classified as an internal treasury operation without relevance to French banking regulation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_contigency_protocol: Maintain a committed stand-by credit facility or overdraft (découvert) equivalent to at least one month of drift to compensate FX-transaction lags and payment-capacity interruptions from the EMI; in addition, open a second EMI counterparty (e.g., Checkout.com) to eliminate single-processor settlement risk.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.tax_documentation_for_cross_border_flows: For each inbound injection, a capital-increase tax form (CERFA 2767-SD) must be filed within one month, and if shares are issued without cash, an independent valuation report is required. For outbound dividends, use DCF (Déclaration de distribution) form 2561 and remit the withholding tax to DGFiP; for cross-border interest payments, apply the applicable interest-barrier rules and certification under Article 125 A.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual data confirmation (confirmation annuelle) of RNE/RCS registration data, including certification of UBO information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI — Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days following the annual anniversary of the RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of Kbis issuance; amicable formal notice from the Greffe; judicial injunction with coercive penalty (astreinte) up to EUR 300 per day; administrative fine up to EUR 10,000; repeated default triggers court-ordered strike-off (radiation) from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory annual general meeting of shareholders (AGM) approving the annual accounts (décision collective des associés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Minutes recorded in the mandatory corporate decision register; enforcement by the President of the Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (Art. L.223-26 Code de commerce); extension up to 6 additional months obtainable by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any interested party may petition the court to compel the meeting; manager exposed to coercive order and personal civil liability for resulting losses; aggregation with non-filing of accounts triggers injunction and strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts at the RCS (balance sheet, profit and loss account, annexes, plus statutory auditor's report when audit is compulsory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via INPI Guichet unique des formalités
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the AGM approving the accounts, and no later than 7 months after fiscal year-end if no court extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order compelling filing within 30 days under threat of astreinte; administrative fine up to EUR 10,000; referral by the Public Prosecutor; ultimate radiation from the RCS for persistent failure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax package (liasse fiscale: Form 2065 and 2050 to 2068 series) with annual results declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than May 3 following calendar year-end (applicable to calendar-year accounts); within 3 months after close for non-calendar fiscal years; mandatory electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 10% late-filing penalty on the assessed tax; late payment interest of 0.20% per month; 40% surcharge for bad faith and 80% for deliberate concealment; exposure to tax audit and enforced recovery

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO register rectification declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) upon share transfer triggering change in beneficial ownership or crossing of 10% capital or voting rights
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI — Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via Guichet unique des formalités
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of the date of the transfer or the change in beneficial ownership (Art. R.561-4-1 Code monétaire et financier)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Blocking of related RNE formalities and Kbis issuance for the new legal situation; administrative fine up to EUR 10,000 per breach; manager's personal liability for non-regularization

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CFE (cotisation foncière des entreprises) local business tax — annual declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP — Service des Impôts des Entreprises (collecting public accountant)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Assessment notice issued between August and November; payment due no later than December 15 of the current year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic taxation based on recognized rental value where no return filed; 10% late-payment surcharge plus 0.20% monthly interest; 40% surcharge for intentional omission; enforced recovery procedure by the public accountant

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux comptes) when the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds at year-end: total balance sheet EUR 6,000,000; net turnover exclusive of tax EUR 12,000,000; average workforce of 50 employees — per Decree No. 2023-393 (Art. R.821-1 Code de commerce). Mandatory also where the SARL is a parent company controlling an entity reaching those limits. Below thresholds: voluntary appointment allowed and prudent for investor-backed companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French statutory accounts under the Plan Comptable Général (ANC Regulation No. 2014-03, as amended), with simplified presentation available for micro-entities per ANC Regulation No. 2016-07. IFRS is permitted only for consolidated accounts of listed groups; individual statutory accounts of the SARL must be prepared under French GAAP and filed as the liasse fiscale with the DGFiP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual confirmation filed through the Guichet unique certifies that the beneficial-ownership data inscribed in the RNE are complete and accurate. For share transfers, the manager must file a rectificative RBE declaration within 15 days of the transfer when the operation modifies the UBO list or causes a person to exceed 10% of share capital or voting rights. The RBE data, together with all underlying declarations, must be physically retained at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des décisions des associés — mandatory shareholder decisions and minute book for SARL covering AGM resolutions, written consultations and unanimous decisions
Registre des mouvements de titres — chronological record of each transfer of parts sociales with dates, parties, and number of shares transferred
Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) — beneficial ownership register kept at the registered office and matching the declaration filed with the RNE

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500-1,600 per year (EUR 450-1,500), covering domiciliation at an approved service provider or accountant, annual confirmation handling, Kbis renewals and RCS correspondence
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500-17,000 (EUR 5,000-15,500), typical market range for a small or medium-sized French SARL statutory audit engagement with PropTech SaaS revenue streams

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate effective 1 January 2022; fiscal years ended on or after 31 December 2022).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit for SMEs (turnover < EUR 10M, fully paid capital); Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% on R&D expenses up to EUR 100M and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% for SMEs; JEI (young innovative enterprise) 3-year CIT relief; patent box at 10% on qualifying nexus-based IP income; CIR/CII refundable on demand for SMEs.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry); annual offset cap: EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit above EUR 1,000,000. Alternative 3-year carryback of up to EUR 1,000,000 creates a tax credit (report en arrière).
